title: Introducing Crumb: A Daily Term-Guessing Game for NEET, JEE, CLAT and More
description: Crumb is Studyloaf's daily puzzle: guess a real subject term in 6 tries with colored letter feedback. One puzzle a day in each of 8 subject domains, plus a shareable result grid.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: We just added a new free tool to Studyloaf: Crumb, a daily term-guessing puzzle built specifically for exam prep instead of general vocabulary. Here's what it is and how to play.

content.heading: What Crumb actually is
content.body: Crumb works like a letter-guessing puzzle you may have played before: guess a word in 6 tries, and after each guess, every letter gets colored feedback showing whether it's in the right spot, in the word but the wrong spot, or not in the word at all. The difference is what you're guessing. Every target word is a real, domain-specific technical term, pulled from an actual exam syllabus, not a common English word picked for letter variety. A clue (the term's topic, e.g. "Cell Division" or "Circuit Theory") is shown throughout the puzzle, so the challenge is genuinely about knowing the term, not about guessing blind.

image.alt: A Crumb NEET puzzle three guesses in, topic Biomolecules: PURINE, AMINES and LYSINE are entered with each letter coloured to show whether it's in the right spot, in the word elsewhere, or not in the word
image.caption: Three guesses into a NEET puzzle. Green means the right letter in the right spot, tan means it's in the term but elsewhere, grey means it's not in the term. The on-screen keyboard tracks every letter you've tried.

content.heading: Why a clue, when the original format doesn't have one
content.body: A pure letter-frequency guessing game tests something different from subject knowledge: it rewards knowing which letters are statistically common in English, not knowing what a term means. For a word like ESTOPPEL or MITOCHONDRIA, guessing blind from zero information isn't a useful test of anything. Showing the topic up front shifts the challenge to where it belongs: once you know which corner of the syllabus it's from, can you land on the exact term, spelled correctly, under a limited number of guesses.

content.heading: Eight domains, one puzzle a day each
content.body: Crumb launched with three word banks (NEET, CLAT and Board Exams) and now has eight, each with its own daily puzzle: NEET (Biology terminology), JEE (Physics, Chemistry and Maths), CLAT (legal terminology), Board Exams (Class 10 to 12 science and maths), ECE (electronics and communication), CS (computer science), AIML (AI and machine learning), and Placements and Aptitude. Each domain gets one attempt per day, and the target term changes daily, so it's a quick, low-effort habit rather than something that eats your study time.

content.heading: Why this actually helps exam prep
content.body: Recognizing a term when you see it in a passage is a different skill from producing it once you're only told which topic it belongs to, and the second skill is closer to what NEET, JEE, CLAT, board exams and placement tests actually test through fill-in-the-blank, matching, and short-answer questions. A minute a day spent retrieving a term from just its subject area, rather than re-reading a glossary, is active recall in a genuinely low-stakes, low-time-cost form.

Your streak and progress are saved automatically, and once you finish a puzzle, you can copy a shareable result grid (built from simple block characters, no account required to view or copy it) that shows your guess pattern without giving away the actual word. Head to the games hub to pick a domain and try today's puzzle.
